summary: Tested Phase 2 (bundled MapLibre map fix) and Phase 3 (EN/Telugu/Hindi localization) changes. Backend pytest 15/15 passing (previously-flagged Gemini daily-quota issue is now fixed via automatic Emergent-key fallback, confirmed live in backend logs: Gemini 429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED -> falls back to gpt-5.6-luna transparently, chat still returns 200 with full verdict/widgets). Manually verified via direct API calls: native-script Hindi query returns fluent Hindi UNSAFE reply citing IMD; romanized Telugu query ('Repu sea loki vellacha?') returns natural casual romanized-Telugu reply — both match requested tone. Language Picker modal (EN/Telugu/Hindi with native labels + checkmark) works. Switching to Telugu fully translates Chat tab (nav labels, quick prompts, placeholder, empty state) with no restart needed — verified via DOM text assertions. Saved and Alerts tabs also translate their static labels (SAVE LOCATION, ASK, GEOFENCE, section headers, empty states). Region switcher regression-checked and working. On web preview, MapWidget correctly shows the intended graceful 'Map failed to load + RETRY' fallback (WebView is an unsupported platform on web by design) instead of a blank map — could NOT verify actual native map rendering since no native/mobile (Expo Go / simulator) testing path was available in this environment; this remains unverified for the original reported real-device bug.

minor.issue: When the app language preference (LanguagePicker -> 'language' field sent to /api/chat) is set to Hindi/Telugu but the user types a genuinely English sentence (e.g. 'Is it safe tomorrow?'), the Planner detects the message's actual language as English and replies in English, ignoring the app-wide language preference (lang_hint is documented as 'fallback only if ambiguous', so this is by design, not a crash). This may not match the review request's expectation that selecting Hindi in the UI should make ALL AI replies Hindi regardless of input script -- confirmed via direct API test (language='hi' + English text -> meta.language='en'). Flagging as a product-behavior decision point, not a bug fix demand.

ui_bugs.component: Alerts screen title, Saved screen title, Alerts section headers (ACTIVE HAZARDS/NOTIFICATIONS)
ui_bugs.issue: HIGH: When lang='te' (and likely 'hi'), the bold uppercase header titles (style has letterSpacing:2, and section titles letterSpacing:1) visually break/garble Telugu conjunct consonants and matras (letter-spacing inserts visual gaps between combining glyph clusters that must stay joined in Indic scripts). The underlying DOM text is correct ('సేవ్‌లు', 'హెచ్చరికలు') but the RENDERED text is visually distorted/hard-to-read for native speakers -- confirmed via screenshot on Saved & Alerts tab headers/section titles in Telugu. This is a real i18n rendering bug, not a false positive: letterSpacing should be disabled (or reduced) for te/hi text throughout the app (headers, tab bar labels, section titles) since Telugu/Devanagari scripts are not designed for character-level letter-spacing.

integration_issues.issue: Toast strings in saved.tsx (e.g. 'Location permission needed...', 'Using your current location', 'Could not get location', 'No matching location found', 'Search unavailable (offline)', 'Coordinates filled from...', 'Enter a name and valid coordinates', 'Location saved', 'Could not save (offline)', 'BREACH: ...', 'Clear — no boundary breach', 'Geofence check failed (offline)') are hardcoded English strings, not run through t()/STRINGS -- they stay in English even when Telugu/Hindi is selected. Static labels (buttons, headers, placeholders) ARE translated correctly; only these dynamic feedback toasts were missed.

react_native_issues.issue: As expected/documented, react-native-webview is an unsupported platform on web, so the map always shows 'Map failed to load' + RETRY after the 9s timeout in this browser-based test environment. This is the correct graceful-degradation behavior per the fix description, NOT a regression. However, this test agent had no native/Expo-Go/simulator path available, so the actual originally-reported real-device bug (map never rendering) could NOT be directly re-verified end-to-end; only the bundled-local-asset code path and the retry/timeout/postMessage logic were reviewed and look correct (MAPLIBRE_JS_ASSET/CSS loaded via expo-asset+expo-file-system, inlined into WebView HTML, postMessage ready/error signaling, 9s timeout, retry button all present and correctly wired in MapWidget.tsx).

action_items: HIGH: Fix letterSpacing-induced visual corruption of Telugu (and check Hindi) native-script text in uppercase bold headers/section titles (alerts.tsx, saved.tsx, and any other letterSpacing-styled Text using t()) -- e.g. conditionally drop letterSpacing when lang !== 'en', or apply it only to the English fallback string.
MEDIUM: Translate the remaining hardcoded-English toast messages in saved.tsx (permission, search, save, geofence feedback strings) into the STRINGS/t() system for te/hi.

LOW/PRODUCT DECISION: Decide whether selecting a language in LanguagePicker should force ALL AI chat replies into that language regardless of the script the user actually types in, or keep current behavior (detect actual input language, app language as tiebreaker only). Current implementation replies in English if the user types genuinely English text even when Hindi/Telugu is selected as app language.
Verify real native-device map rendering via Expo Go/simulator when such a testing path becomes available -- not verifiable from this web-only test environment.
critical_code_review_comments: agents.py's Gemini->Emergent-key fallback (_chat_with_fallback) fully resolves the CRITICAL quota-exhaustion issue flagged in iteration_3 -- confirmed live via backend logs showing automatic recovery from a 429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED Gemini error to a successful gpt-5.6-luna completion within the same request, with verdict/widgets/citations intact.

MapWidget.tsx: bundling MapLibre JS/CSS as local assets (expo-asset + expo-file-system) instead of a CDN <script src> is a sound architectural fix for the reported real-device bug; code review shows correct fallback (in-memory caching, Promise reuse to avoid duplicate downloads, graceful null on failure reverting to CDN tags) plus proper postMessage ready/error handshake and timeout/retry UX.
AppContext.tsx STRINGS dictionary is clean and DRY (all 3 languages co-located per key) -- good practice, but coverage gap noted above (toast strings in saved.tsx bypass STRINGS entirely).

success_rate.frontend: ~90% of testable flows (chat localization, saved/alerts translation, region switcher regression, map fallback UX all working); native map rendering fix unverifiable in this web-only environment; 1 confirmed i18n rendering bug (letterSpacing on Telugu headers)

seed_data_creation: No persistent test data left (TEST_ prefixed session/user ids used in manual verification script, no DB writes beyond ephemeral chat/session records).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Gemini quota fallback confirmed fixed and working -- no longer a blocker for chat testing. New HIGH-priority finding this round: letterSpacing on bold uppercase headers/section-titles visually breaks Telugu (and possibly Hindi) native script rendering (screenshots in /tmp/saved_header_te.png, /tmp/alerts_header_te.png during this session, not persisted). Also confirmed several Saved-screen toast messages are un-translated hardcoded English. MapWidget's actual native-device rendering fix remains UNVERIFIED end-to-end since no native/Expo-Go testing path exists in this sandbox -- only code review + web fallback-UX (retry button) were confirmed; recommend a native device/simulator check before closing that ticket.
rca_of_issue: letterSpacing bug RCA: Text.style.letterSpacing (used in title/sectionTitle styles across alerts.tsx, saved.tsx, and tabBarLabelStyle in _layout.tsx) is applied uniformly to translated strings without regard to script. CSS/RN letter-spacing inserts uniform space between EVERY character/grapheme cluster boundary; Telugu and Devanagari are complex scripts where consonant+vowel-sign (matra) or consonant-conjunct sequences must render as tightly joined glyph clusters -- inserting spacing between them breaks the visual shaping, making text look garbled/wrong even though the underlying string is correct. Reproduced by switching app language to Telugu and screenshotting the Saved and Alerts tab headers/section titles.
